note: Found by the same oracle: the alias timeline read the `ns` form's clauses and nothing else, so every TOP-LEVEL `require` was invisible — `jio` at core.clj:7248, plus `str/replace` and `ns/find-namespaces-in-dir`, were the three surviving misses. Reading only the unquoted `(require [lib :as a])` finds nothing in real code, because nobody writes that: the quote IS the convention. A top-level require's children are the SPEC VECS themselves, where an `ns` form's clauses hold them, so one spec reader has to serve both shapes. Pins all three alias keys resolve: `:as` at :14 and :15, and the positional `:as-alias` — which has no `:as` keyword to read — at :26.
